scientific_hypothesis: A periodic HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave Bragg stack with center wavelength tuned to the visible band will achieve high reflectance at 400-700 nm while maintaining high transmittance at 1530-1565 nm.
expected_advantages: Predictable spectral position from quarter-wave wavelength
L33 validates cold mirror concept for visible-reflect/IR-transmit
known_risks: Periodic structure may have limited band-edge sharpness
Passband ripple from impedance mismatch at air interface
May not achieve both bands simultaneously with fixed pair count
expected_observations: If hypothesis holds: best_target_score should increase as reference wavelength approaches 550 nm (visible band center), with valid_candidates remaining stable across rounds
If hypothesis fails: best_target_score should plateau below 0.7 regardless of reference wavelength, indicating periodic structure cannot satisfy both bands simultaneously
tightest_margin should remain positive if both bands are achievable with this topology
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
If valid_candidates drops to zero for three consecutive rounds, relax the quarter-wave constraint and stop
